DXS2 in plastidic MEP pathway; controls isoprenoid (including GA/CK) biosynthesis and chloroplast development, strongly linked to growth and stem elongation.
Dicer-like involved in 21-nt siRNAs and ta-siRNAs that regulate ARF/auxin pathways and shoot architecture; good developmental regulator candidate.
Ethylene-responsive TF; integrates stress and ethylene signaling known to modulate stem elongation and growth–defense trade-offs.
LRR receptor-like kinase; plausible regulator of hormone or peptide signaling influencing cell expansion and meristem activity.
Kinesin-like protein; cytoskeleton/organelle dynamics may impact cell elongation and organ growth, though mechanism is less specific than AHA9/DXS2.
Organellar transcription termination; affects chloroplast and mitochondrial function and thus overall vigor and size, but not stem-specific.
Controls thylakoid curvature and photosynthetic efficiency; may influence biomass and stem length via general photosynthetic capacity.
Required for cytochrome b6 maturation and photosynthetic electron transport; impacts energy supply and growth, indirectly affecting stem length.
PPi-dependent phosphofructokinase; central carbon metabolism, could modulate growth rate but highly pleiotropic.
Mitochondrial small HSP; stress-responsive chaperone that may influence growth under stress conditions.
Peroxisomal Lon protease; protein quality control and metabolic homeostasis, potentially influencing growth under stress.
Vesicle transport protein; ER–Golgi trafficking may affect delivery of wall components or receptors, but link to stem length is indirect.
Core splicing factor; global effects on gene expression and development, growth phenotypes possible but not stem-specific.
PPR protein; organellar RNA metabolism; can affect vigor and development but mechanism for stem-specific variation is unclear.
Ribosomal protein; general translation; variation could change overall growth rate but very pleiotropic.
PPR protein; as above, likely affects organelle gene expression and overall vigor rather than specific stem elongation pathways.
Defense-related TF; may influence growth through SA/JA trade-offs, especially under stress conditions.
Defense/stress-associated membrane protein; plausible growth–defense trade-off effects but no clear stem-specific mechanism.
O-fucosyltransferase; may modify receptors or secreted proteins involved in growth signaling; mechanistic link is speculative.
60S ribosomal export factor; essential for protein synthesis and growth, but very general.
Best hit is a mouse telomere protein with low query coverage; likely spurious domain-level match rather than a true plant ortholog.
Coronavirus replicase polyprotein; almost certainly spurious alignment, not a genuine plant gene driving stem length.
Bacterial small HSP; likely a conserved domain hit; limited relevance for interpreting plant stem length variation.
Animal protein of unknown function; low identity/coverage; unlikely to be informative for plant stem length.
